Bubble-swarm plot of a census against the no-difference line

Source: R/swarm.R
plot_swarm.Rd

One row per census. Each bubble is one distinct estimate among the counted alternative analyses (rounded to digits), with area proportional to the number of analyses giving that value and shade by the share of those analyses that are significant; bubbles holding five or more analyses are numbered. A ring marks the pre-specified estimate, the shaded band holds the central 95% of the distinct values, the heavy vertical line is no difference, and the least favourable alternative is labelled. Deletions are a strip of small light dots beneath the swarm.

Usage

plot_swarm(
  x,
  scale = c("percent", "estimate"),
  digits = 2,
  r0 = 0.004,
  favours = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  xlim = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A stress_census, or a named list of them (one row each, drawn on a shared axis; the first is drawn at the top).

scale

"percent" draws estimates as a percent of the pre-specified estimate, so several endpoints share an axis; "estimate" uses the response units (only sensible for one census or censuses on one scale).

digits

Rounding used to decide which estimates are "the same value".

r0

Radius of a count-one bubble as a fraction of the x-axis range.

favours

Labels for the two sides of no difference, in the order (reference arm, active arm). Defaults to the treatment level names.

xlab

Axis label; NULL for a default.

xlim

Axis limits; NULL for automatic limits that include zero.

Value

A ggplot object (uses a fixed aspect ratio so bubbles are round).

Examples

spec <- stress_spec(mmrm::fev_data, "FEV1", "USUBJID", "AVISIT", "ARMCD", "PBO",
                    covariates = ~ RACE + SEX + FEV1_BL)
cen <- stress_census(spec, stress_covariance(spec, c("us", "cs", "ar1h", "toep")),
                     stress_covariates(spec), stress_loo(spec, by = "RACE"))
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) plot_swarm(cen)
